subject: nextjs
summary: Explains Next.js App Router file conventions, folder-to-URL mapping, dynamic routes, route groups, and layout nesting for navigating project structure.
key_points: App Router uses file-system-based routing — folder structure maps to URL paths.
Special files (page.tsx, layout.tsx, loading.tsx, error.tsx) each serve a specific role.
Route groups (parentheses) organize files without affecting URLs; dynamic routes (brackets) capture URL segments.
misconceptions: A folder without page.tsx still creates a routable URL.
Route groups like (marketing) appear in the URL path.
Layout files only affect the immediate page, not nested routes.
check_questions: What is the role of page.tsx vs layout.tsx in App Router?
How do dynamic route segments [param] work?
What happens when you access a path with no page.tsx?

fact_candidates: App Router file naming conventions and their roles
practical_judgment_candidates: Deciding when to use a route group vs a regular folder
Choosing where to place a layout for shared navigation
scenario_candidates: Reading folder structure to predict URLs and layout scope
Dynamic route parameter extraction from URL
common_wrong_answer_patterns: Assuming route groups are part of the URL
Believing a folder alone creates a routable page
